views.label: Source evidence
views.note: Capture preserves exact source evidence; parsing interprets content without rewriting its raw identity.

views.label: Content versioning
views.note: Deterministic normalization produces the canonical fingerprint; only CREATE_VERSION writes a new version and chunks.

views.label: Access governance
views.note: Access changes may refresh current permissions independently, including before new content is persisted.

views.label: Persistence and replay
views.note: SQLite records source captures, ingestion runs, state and evidence; completed identical captures are replay-safe.

cards.title: 1 · Preserve source evidence
items: Source identity, source version, exact bytes, capture timestamp and access policy are retained as provenance; source_version alone does not define a content version.
Supported parsers handle UTF-8 text, Markdown, HTML and DOCX deterministically; PDF/OCR and model-assisted parsing are not part of this implemented path.
Parser output becomes canonical evidence without replacing raw capture; unsupported formats and malformed documents fail explicitly.

cards.title: 2 · Decide whether content changed
items: Normalize presentation noise (for example line endings, trailing spaces and repeated blank lines) before fingerprinting the canonical title and ordered blocks.
First-seen content or a different canonical fingerprint => CREATE_VERSION: materialize a KnowledgeDocument, chunk it and persist the new version.
Same canonical content and unchanged access => NO_CONTENT_VERSION: no new content version or chunks.
Normalization strategy changed => REBASELINE_REQUIRED: require deliberate rebaselining rather than treating a new algorithm as a content edit.

cards.title: 3 · Update access independently
items: Access fingerprint is computed separately from content, using tenant ID, authorization scope and allowed groups.
Same content with changed access => REFRESH_GOVERNANCE without creating chunks.
When both content and access change, governance refresh can run before CREATE_VERSION; state checks reject unexpected concurrent changes.
Each run records stage, outcome and failure details. The diagram is a synchronous ingestion view, not a deployed API or complete retrieval architecture.

cards.title: 4 · Replay, durability and audit
items: SQLite persists immutable source captures, run stages and outcomes, current canonical state, document versions, and governed chunks.
A completed capture with the same knowledge ID and ingestion fingerprint returns its prior result instead of performing the work again.
Expected-state checks surface competing canonical updates rather than silently overwriting a newer version; failures are recorded by stage.
